21: D is correct because it combines an S3-hosted static site with a CloudFront distribution for edge caching, which delivers millisecond latency to millions of requests per hour without any servers to manage, while API Gateway and Lambda provide a fully managed, auto-scaling backend and DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. This serverless architecture has essentially no operational overhead and scales automatically to absorb the hourly traffic spikes of a one-deal-a-day model.
22: B is correct because S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent access and infrequent access tiers based on changing access patterns with no retrieval fees, which directly addresses the unpredictable mix of frequently and rarely accessed files while minimizing storage costs. It also stores objects redundantly across multiple Availability Zones, satisfying the resilience requirement. The fixed-pattern options either cost more for unpredictable workloads or, in the case of One Zone-IA, do not survive the loss of an Availability Zone.
23: B is correct because an S3 Lifecycle rule transitioning objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month matches the access pattern exactly: files are hot for one month and then never accessed again, but must be kept indefinitely. Glacier Deep Archive has the lowest storage cost of any S3 storage class, roughly a quarter the price of Standard-IA, making it the most cost-effective choice for permanent archival of data with no retrieval expectations.
24: B is correct because Cost Explorer is the native, fully managed AWS Billing tool that supports granular filtering, including by instance type, service, and tags, letting the solutions architect graph and compare the last two months of EC2 costs and drill down to find which instance types drove the vertical scaling. It requires no infrastructure, reports, or additional tooling, giving the in-depth analysis with the least operational overhead.
25: D is correct because splitting the workload into two Lambda functions decoupled by an SQS queue lets the ingestion function accept data immediately and buffer it durably, while the loading function pulls from the queue at a rate the database can handle, so Lambda concurrency quotas are no longer a bottleneck. SQS provides built-in retry and dead-letter handling, and each function stays within default quotas, improving scalability with minimal configuration effort.
26: A is correct because AWS Config records the configuration of S3 buckets over time and, with the appropriate managed rules such as s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited or s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only, continuously evaluates buckets against desired configurations and can detect and alert on unauthorized configuration changes. This provides a complete, auditable configuration history with no custom code, whereas logging services only record access events rather than compliance of configuration changes.
27: A is correct because CloudWatch dashboards can be shared directly from the console with specific email addresses or via a shareable link that requires an IAM identity, providing read-only access to people who do not have an AWS account or IAM credentials. This grants the product manager periodic access to exactly that one dashboard and nothing else, satisfying least privilege without creating extra IAM users, broader console access, or any infrastructure to operate.
28: B is correct because AWS SSO (now IAM Identity Center) provides single sign-on across all accounts in AWS Organizations, and connecting it to the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory through AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory with a two-way forest trust lets users continue to be managed in on-premises AD while gaining access to all AWS accounts. The two-way trust allows both directory sides to reference each other, which is the standard supported configuration for this SSO scenario.
29: A is correct because a Network Load Balancer is required since only the NLB handles UDP traffic, and registering the NLB as an endpoint in AWS Global Accelerator routes users over the AWS global network to the closest healthy Region with the lowest latency and provides automatic failover to another Region if an endpoint becomes unhealthy. This combination is purpose-built for multi-Region, latency-sensitive, non-HTTP workloads such as VoIP.
30: C is correct because creating a snapshot when tests finish, terminating the DB instance, and restoring it from the snapshot when needed means the company pays for the DB instance only during the roughly 48 hours of monthly testing plus inexpensive snapshot storage for the rest of the month, while the restored instance retains the exact same compute and memory attributes. Simply stopping the instance would still incur full storage and licensing charges, and changing instance classes or scaling would alter the compute and memory attributes, so the snapshot approach is the most cost-effective.
31: A is correct because AWS Config provides a managed rule, required-tags, that automatically detects when EC2 instances, RDS DB instances, and Redshift clusters are launched or reconfigured without the required tags, and it continuously evaluates the entire account and reports noncompliant resources in a dashboard. This requires no custom code, scheduling, or manual reviews, minimizing both configuration and operational effort.
32: B is correct because an S3 bucket can directly host a static website consisting of HTML, CSS, client-side JavaScript, and images with no compute resources to provision, patch, or pay for. S3 website hosting charges only for storage and requests, making it dramatically cheaper and simpler than running containers in Fargate, an EC2 web server, or an ALB with Lambda.
33: C is correct because Kinesis Data Streams provides a highly scalable, near-real-time ingestion layer for millions of transactions, and a Lambda function consuming the stream can strip sensitive data before writing each transaction to DynamoDB for low-latency document retrieval. Other internal applications can independently consume the same live stream to receive transaction details in near real time, which decouples producers from consumers and meets every stated requirement.
34: B is correct because AWS Config is the service designed to track configuration changes on AWS resources over time, while AWS CloudTrail is the service that records the history of API calls made to those resources for auditing. This pairing is the standard AWS answer for configuration tracking plus API call recording, whereas CloudWatch collects metrics and logs rather than configuration state or API history.
35: D is correct because AWS Shield Advanced provides advanced detection and mitigation for large-scale, sophisticated DDoS attacks, includes 24/7 DDoS response team support and cost protection, and can explicitly protect an Elastic Load Balancer, which is the internet-facing resource in this architecture. Standard Shield is automatically enabled at no charge but does not offer the advanced protections and support needed for a deliberate large-scale attack defense.
36: B is correct because a customer managed multi-Region KMS key is a single logical key with replicable key material in both Regions, so the application can encrypt and decrypt data in both S3 buckets with the same key while the data and key material are present in each Region. Using the multi-Region key with client-side encryption is what allows the identical key to be used across Regions, since a standard regional KMS key cannot be referenced outside its own Region, and this design meets the requirement with minimal ongoing management.
37: B is correct because AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides encrypted remote shell sessions to EC2 instances through IAM roles with no open inbound ports, no bastion hosts, no SSH key management, and no VPN, and it logs sessions for auditing, aligning with the Well-Architected security pillar. Attaching an IAM role to each instance is a simple, repeatable, native process with the least operational overhead.
38: C is correct because an Amazon CloudFront distribution caches the static website content at edge locations worldwide, significantly decreasing latency for global users, and it requires no replication of data to multiple Regions. For a static S3 website this is the most cost-effective approach since it needs only one distribution and one bucket, whereas replicating buckets to every Region or using Global Accelerator costs more and is not designed for caching static content.
39: A is correct because the diagnosed problem is storage performance: a 2 TB General Purpose SSD (gp2) volume delivers a fixed baseline of IOPS that, with millions of daily updates on a 10 million row table, has its I/O capacity exhausted, causing long insert waits. Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) delivers a guaranteed, consistent level of IOPS well above the gp2 baseline, directly fixing the storage bottleneck. Changing instance class would address compute or memory, not disk throughput, and read replicas only offload reads.
40: A is correct because Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, highly available ingestion service that automatically scales to capture 1 TB of daily alerts with no infrastructure to run, and it delivers the data directly to an S3 bucket where an S3 Lifecycle rule automatically transitions objects older than 14 days to Glacier for low-cost archiving. This keeps the most recent 14 days immediately available in S3 for analysis while automating archival, all with zero servers to manage.
